turns.input: *He punches Bartolomhew directly in the face.*
turns.narration:
Bartolomhew's easy smile flickers as your fist meets his jaw. His head snaps back with a soft grunt, and he staggers half a step on the packed earth of the market square, one hand rising to his face. Around you, a few nearby handlers and a bored-looking guard pause to watch, but no one moves to intervene in what appears to be a private dispute among buyers.

He touches his split lip, examines the blood on his fingertips with mild curiosity, then meets your eyes again. The warmth in his voice remains, though it's thinned now, more measuring.

"Ah." A small laugh, almost admiring. "I had wondered what kind of man takes a dead woman's tower without asking after her debts. Now I know." He straightens his clerical collar with his unbloodied hand, glancing past you toward the auction pens as if contemplating whether to continue this conversation. "That will cost you extra, you understand. The documentation, I mean. Clerks don't care for visible injury at point of sale."

turns.scene_section:
[CURRENT AUTHORITATIVE SCENE]
Location: Calderan Slave Market. A public, legal slave market in Calderan's West District, publicly known, about 20 minutes' walk from Heartstone. Its very large square exceeds Main Market Square: practical packed earth, gravel and dirt, muddy in poor weather, sometimes dirtied by blood and animal/human traffic. This major economic center has heavy daytime traffic: buyers, sellers, slaves, caravans, handlers, clerks, guards, spectators and auctions. Slavery is legal and socially accepted; ordinary attendance is not clandestine. The complex operates around the clock, formal auctions primarily by day, direct purchases outside auction hours, much less activity at night. The general authorized public auction has no named operator. Low-level authorized clerks handle required ownership documentation at official auction sales; licensed private sellers handle or arrange their own authorized sale documentation. No routine health certification requirement is established; no systematic doctors or medical inspection are present. Licensed sellers behind/around the auction conduct private acquisitions: Korvin is generalist, Mistress Elara handles prestigious and socially useful captives, Bartolomhew specializes in Beastfolk and labor/workforce categories. They do not operate the public auction. The taboo Back Alleys and deeper criminal layer are distinct. No dominant origin or percentages: sources may include war prisoners, convicted criminals, hereditary slavery, debt, economic ruin, refugees, criminal trafficking, vulnerable Beastfolk, captured elves, bandit/criminal-associated captives and other legally processed or illicitly laundered captives. Not every refugee, Beastfolk or elf is enslaved.

He was transported into this world from another world approximately one day before the campaign begins, and he has essentially no prior lived knowledge of this world unless explicitly established later. On arrival he became the lawful owner/holder of Heartstone Tower. He is tall and overweight, with a few visible white hairs and very mild, early balding; no further appearance details are established. His magical affinity/school is Light. His currently known Light subschools are healing and sacrifice, understood only within the existing magic framework; no mechanics for sacrifice are established.
